Claude — Daily Rhythm & Confessions: how the Church ends the day — an honest look back and confession before sleep, instead of the phone (39 - HOW THE DAY SHOULD END)

Claude — History & the Saints: Saint Nicholas of Myra and the three bags of gold — the bishop behind the most public gift-giving season wanted his giving hidden; secret alms, Matthew 6:3 (40 - THE BISHOP WHO GAVE IN SECRET)

Claude — Places & Journeys: Patmos — the small Aegean island where tradition says Rome exiled John and where the Church remembers the Revelation was given; the place you call exile may be where you finally hear Him; Revelation 1:9 (41 - THE ROCK THEY SENT HIM TO)

Claude — Hard Questions: isn't faith just a crutch for weak men? He agrees — every man leans on something; Paul boasted of his weakness (2 Corinthians 12:9-10); the shame is not the crutch but limping and calling it strength (42 - ISN'T FAITH A CRUTCH FOR WEAK MEN)

Claude — Practical Wisdom: what actually happens the first time a man walks into an Orthodox church — stand at the back, light a candle, stay in place at the chalice, take the blessed bread; the real fear is being seen not knowing, which is pride; Psalm 122:1 (43 - YOUR FIRST TIME IN AN ORTHODOX CHURCH)

Claude — Reading the Culture: the irony culture — everything is a joke so nobody has to defend anything; irony is armour against being caught caring, and a man who means nothing cannot promise, repent or pray; Proverbs 26:19, Matthew 5:37 (44 - THE MAN WHO JOKES ABOUT EVERYTHING)

Claude — Daily Rhythm & Confessions: the icon corner — every man already has an altar in his room (the desk and the screen); Orthodox homes kept a corner facing east with an icon and a lamp, the "red corner", where red also meant beautiful; build one corner and show up to it; Matthew 6:6 (45 - THE CORNER OF YOUR ROOM)

Claude — Mysteries & Wonders: St Seraphim of Sarov and Nicholas Motovilov in the snow, November 1831: by Motovilov's own written account Seraphim's face became brighter than the sun; in the same conversation Seraphim said prayer, fasting and good works are only the means, and the aim of the Christian life is to acquire the Holy Spirit of God; the disciplines are the tools, not the treasure; Matthew 17:2, Galatians 5:22 (46 - THE FACE BRIGHTER THAN THE SUN)
